post.title: Do your taxes fund the Federal Reserve? Not quite.
post.ig:
Your taxes don't pay for the Federal Reserve.
Congress doesn't fund it. Its income comes mainly from interest on the bonds it holds, plus fees for services to banks.
After costs, it sends leftover profit to the Treasury: $107.4 billion in 2021.
In 2025 it earned $155.3 billion in interest but paid out $167.4 billion. Losses are booked as a deferred asset, about $233 billion as of Sept 30, 2026, repaid from future profits before most remittances resume.
Sources: Federal Reserve (2021 results, 2025 financial statements, H.4.1 Oct 1, 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
Is the Federal Reserve funded by taxpayers? No: it earns interest on the bonds it holds and fees for bank services, and sent $107.4 billion in profit to the Treasury in 2021. Since late 2022 its interest costs have topped its income, and it books losses as a deferred asset, about $233 billion as of Sept 30, 2026 (Fed H.4.1), repaid from future profits.
